metadata.description: Custom Claude Code plugins — multi-phase AI development pipeline (essense-flow + autopilot), living-model steward loop, queryable project knowledge base (kb), data exploration, prompt modifiers, project question tracking, cross-platform alerts, and verifiability-aware work classification.

plugins.name: essense-flow
plugins.description: Multi-phase AI development pipeline. Closed contracts, evidence-bound review, fail-soft hooks, no resource caps. Eleven skills (elicit, research, triage, architect, organize, build, glossary, review, verify, context, heal) drive a state machine from project pitch to shipped code. /organize (post-architect) and /glossary (post-build) are optional DRY phases powered by the plugin-toolkit code-glossary engine; /glossary renders a functionality map (MAP.md) plus per-sprint duplication drift, /architect consults the map before deciding (reuse ledger in ARCH.md), /build dispatches carry existing-helper + neighbor context, and /review gains a glossary-fed dry-violation lens. Every phase-producing skill writes artifact + transitions state atomically. State is artifacts-authoritative: .pipeline/state.yaml is a derived cache that self-reconciles from disk (state-reconcile op; missing cache auto-rebuilds inside ops). Every agent self-report is re-validated against disk — drift is auditable, not silent. Producer agents follow the librarian protocol: what they cannot verify they research, what research cannot answer becomes a structured unknowns[] entry surfaced to the user at phase gates — never assumed. Hooks are advisory: context-inject surfaces phase + canonical paths on every prompt, next-step suggests the recommended slash command on Stop. Both fail-soft on degraded state — never block tool calls. v0.7.0 archived on archive/essense-flow-v0.7.

plugins.name: essense-autopilot
plugins.description: Stop-hook autopilot for essense-flow pipelines. Drives the pipeline forward across phases without you typing between steps. Halts at human gates (eliciting, organizing, glossarying, verifying), real blockers, in-flight background Agent calls (transcript-scan), forward-detect for sprint-complete + QA-REPORT, and no-progress (same phase + sprint + wave as last fire â†’ suggests /heal). Opt-in per project via .pipeline/config.yaml. Diagnostic stderr on every halt path.

plugins.name: schema-scout
plugins.description: CLI tool for exploring the schema and values of any data file (XLSX, CSV, JSON). Auto-detects JSON in cells, repairs double-encoded UTF-8, prunes overflow artifacts.

plugins.name: thorough-mode
plugins.description: Prompt modifiers — keyword triggers (++, @thorough, @ship, @present, @debug, @verify, @fresh, @prompt, @build) that inject behavioral rules for thoroughness, documentation checks, interactive questions, root-cause investigation, paranoid verification, context refresh, next-session kickoff-prompt generation, and plan-review-build change workflows. Smart hints suggest modifiers when you describe the intent without the keyword. @thorough, @fresh, and @prompt injections are protocol-shaped (failure named -> ordered steps -> anti-signals -> exit check); @prompt DRAFT->VERIFY->COLD-READ->SAVE disk-verifies every citation and SAVES each prompt to an append-only .claude/prompts/ history + INDEX.md ledger. @build REVIEW carries a reuse-first gate (already built here, or served by a package? reuse/extend, do not reinvent). @ship integrates with plugin-toolkit (/version-bump + /docs-audit) when used in mk-cc-resources plugin repo.

plugins.name: project-note-tracker
plugins.description: Track questions per handler/department. Auto-detects which handler should answer, researches from project context in the background, logs to an Excel tracker, generates meeting agendas. Auto-gitignores itself.

plugins.name: alert-sounds
plugins.description: Cross-platform alerts for Claude Code events — sound, desktop notifications, status line colors, volume control, and mute/unmute. Fully configurable per event.

plugins.name: session-lifecycle
plugins.description: Session lifecycle tools — handoff (capture session state), resume (restore context from handoff), claude-md-sync (propose CLAUDE.md updates after changes), retro (metrics-driven retrospective), meta-review (diagnose session: multi-step chains, skill friction, plugin coverage gaps). Designed as cohesive set: handoff triggers claude-md-sync when stale, resume reads handoff output, meta-review diagnoses what's worth automating from observed patterns. Handoffs are an append-only history — each /handoff writes a permanent timestamped file + INDEX.md ledger under .claude/handoffs/ (latest mirrored to .claude/handoff.md for /resume); /resume preserves the history instead of truncating it.

plugins.name: plugin-toolkit
plugins.description: Plugin/skill development + maintenance toolkit. /skill-heal audits a plugin's skill set against current best practices (parallel review agents, scorecard, diagnostic only). /plugin-scaffold bootstraps a new plugin with full directory + cross-references (9-step chain in one invocation). /version-bump cascades version updates across plugin.json + marketplace.json + bundle + metadata + RELEASE-NOTES with semver validation. /docs-audit cross-checks CLAUDE.md + README + marketplace.json against disk state and proposes targeted fixes. /code-glossary (v2) audits any codebase for DRY violations — a deterministic Python engine (Python/TS/JS/C# via stdlib AST + tree-sitter) indexes every function, fingerprints 5 signals, and clusters duplicates; in-session sub-agents label against a 147-verb controlled vocabulary, review each cluster (Pass B), substrate-verify instances (Pass C), and judge near-miss candidates generated deterministically. Optional block scanner (--scan-blocks) surfaces duplicated sub-function guard patterns. Writes GLOSSARY.yaml (frozen schema, /dry-refactor input) + GLOSSARY.md; `runner diff` tracks duplication drift between runs by {(file, function)} identity; `runner map` renders MAP.md — a functionality map (mermaid module graph + lossless machine index) consulted before designing or building; `runner coupling` enforces DECOUPLED by measuring coupling on a scope-aware call graph from records — threshold-free binary violations (cross-module dependency cycles + reach-ins into a module's internal surface), `--fail-on-violation` CI gate, COUPLING.yaml names each violation file:function for substrate-verification. /dry-refactor (v3 MVP) turns extractable clusters into reviewable refactor plans: 7 Appendix-A pre-flight gates (baseline tests, git-clean, target module, verification, confidence, substrate-verify, gitignore) + dry-run helper/edit-plan output, zero source writes. Also powers essense-flow's /organize + /glossary phases. Composable — @ship references /version-bump + /docs-audit; /skill-heal hints at /docs-audit when description quality is weak.

plugins.name: verifiability-lens
plugins.description: A strict, opinionated work-quality guardian that fires automatically on your work and pushes it to the best achievable. Runs THREE checks and ACTIVELY verifies (web + docs + read tools — confirms/refutes, not just flags): (1) Verifiability — A (verified/checkable) / B (genuine guess) / U (can't tell; never let a U pass as A); (2) Completeness — was everything meant to be done actually done, or did we stop arbitrarily (presses to continue + finish, tested); (3) Quality bar — tested, requirements met, robust, not half-assed. A surfacing triage (auto-resolve | escalate | suppress) tuned by a recipient profile hands you ONLY the important, actionable, fully-contextualized pushes — strict judgment, disciplined surfacing; never a context-less decision; auto-resolutions logged. Fires on substantive-work turns (code/files, reads, web, subagents, MCP), reading the WHOLE turn; pure questions + its own output never trigger it. Also a /verifiability manual trigger. Read/research-only — verifies and pushes, does not write code or run the build. 0.5.0: its own Stop hook is RETIRED — the trigger now ships as the `quality-lens` duty in the turn-end plugin (install that to get the automatic firing), because the old fire-once guard bounded consecutive blocks rather than total fires and fired 8 times over ONE user request. This plugin no longer carries any hook.

plugins.name: reuse-gate
plugins.description: Reuse-first reminder at the moment code is written. A PreToolUse hook fires ONCE per user message on the first source-code write (Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit) and surfaces the reuse-first checklist — is this already implemented here (search the codebase / functionality glossary MAP.md) or served by an existing package/library? reuse or extend before writing new; what you do write, build modular + decoupled. A deterministic nudge at the exact point of writing, so the rule can't drift out of context the way an instruction can. Mechanism: hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext fires once per user message (dedupe keyed on prompt_id) on the first source write of the turn — injected before the tool runs so the write proceeds normally (no block, no permissionDecision, so your normal write-permission prompt is untouched). Source-only — docs/config/data files never trigger. Opt-in OFF by default (env REUSE_GATE_ENABLED=1 / project or global .claude/reuse-gate.json {"enabled": true}, project overrides global); fail-open on any error. Companion to the reuse-first instructions in essense-flow code-conventions.md, global CLAUDE.md, and thorough-mode @build. Carries a hook — install separately from the mk-cc-all bundle.

plugins.name: steward
plugins.description: The project's living-model keeper — 'the guy behind the inbox.' Per project it maintains a rich model (.steward/: vision, state, parts+contracts, open questions, next tasks) and an inbox your stray thoughts land in; on every input it RECOMPUTES the whole model (adds/edits/deletes, cascades pivots) and shows the diff, so you always know where the ship is and why. Ambient interface, zero commands to remember: opening the project auto-briefs you (SessionStart hook, totally silent in projects without a model), talking normally captures ideas, plain words drive work ('what's next', 'do it'), session leftovers integrate at next open — owner present. /steward:seed builds the model FOR you from an existing project's docs/code/history plus 3-7 quick questions; /steward:brief|sync|next are optional aliases. The steward agent is the only writer of .steward/ and never touches product code; no work happens in your absence (inbox staging only, permanently). Design source: design/continuous-transformation.md v3. Carries a hook — install standalone, not part of the mk-cc-all bundle.

plugins.name: statusline
plugins.description: Segment-based statusline: model | current task | directory | steward anchor (⚓ + inbox count in .steward projects) | context counter (normalized used-% bar — 100% = usable-window limit accounting for the ~16.5% autocompact buffer; green/yellow/orange/skull). Each segment is an independent fail-soft function — extend by dropping a function into SEGMENTS. Statusline is a settings-level surface: wiring is one settings.json statusLine line pointing at bin/mk-statusline.js (see README). No hooks, no skills — install is just the wiring.

plugins.name: kb
plugins.description: The project's queryable knowledge base — the pull surface the long-lens tools (steward, verifiability-lens) have been missing; they push a fixed briefing at session open, kb lets a session ask for what it needs when it needs it. Files knowledge on two orthogonal axes: KIND (which catalog — episodic what-happened, semantic settled-facts, procedural how-we-work; the CoALA taxonomy Letta/Mem0/LangChain share) x CASTE (which scope tier, ordered narrow to wide — session, thread, project, fleet, owner). Indexes the markdown stores a project already keeps (steward model/log/inbox, handoffs, kickoff prompts, CLAUDE.md) with zero config; an append-only ledger splits per ## section so a hit points at the answer, not the file. Every result reports what it held back and which facet separates the remainder — Claude Code has no MCP sampling, so the session itself is the retrieval loop rather than a second agent. Four reach-surfaces over one facade: always-loaded MCP tools (kb_query/kb_read/kb_overview — Claude self-serves knowledge mid-work, ReAct-style, narrowing hints riding inside each tool result; hand-rolled stdio JSON-RPC, ships via plugin .mcp.json), the `kb` skill (ask before re-deriving), the /kb command (you ask), and the CLI (hooks, scripts, cli-agent). 0.3.0 adds create + maintain: /kb-seed extracts an existing project's knowledge (docs, git history, code; depth-mandated sweep, seeder judges then reports, Extracted-from citations) into .claude/kb/extracted/, /kb-capture files one decision/dead-end/finding at a time into .claude/kb/captures/ — per-file frontmatter carries kind/caste/themes so one dir holds mixed kinds; the engine stays read-only, and steward-model changes still route to .steward/inbox/ for recompute. 0.4.0: retrieval rung 1 — light stemming, edit-distance-1 typo tolerance, config alias groups, thin-preamble skip. 0.5.0: the awareness surface — a kb-pull UserPromptSubmit hook (deterministic ranker over the prompt, score-floored one-line hints naming what the KB holds, kb_read to pull; machine-text guarded, config off-switch) + a rolling session digest (.claude/kb/session-digest.md, working-kind session-caste, injected every prompt, capped-loud) + per-call JSONL traces + a config-regex pattern split mode for ledgers whose entries are not headings. 0.6.0: the ENFORCED write side — a kb-scribe Stop hook blocks a producing turn's yield until the session distills it into the digest AND graduates durable knowledge (settled decision/dead-end/finding → .claude/kb/captures/; steward-model change → .steward/inbox/), so one pass feeds both the session-length and project-length memory; it states what IMPORTANT means (the dies-first classes: decision-with-why, rejected approach and what refuted it, verified outcome with its check, constraint, direction change) plus an explicit NOT-important list, sharpened per project by a `scribe.focus` config list; loop-safe via the verifiability-lens contract (fire-exactly-once, hash-skip, own-marker guard, fail-open) and switchable off. No scribe agent by design — the session already holds the turn; only a judge needs independence. Config merging is generic (object knobs patch per key, so a new knob is config, not code). Node only, no dependencies, 256+37+42+56+38+33 tests. 0.7.0: SELF-RUNNING — kb coverage prints the top-up map (which substrate existing entries already cite, where coverage stops) so /kb-seed can be re-run in any project and mines only what is missing; upkeep self-activates on PRESENCE (a project with no curated memory is never blocked — seeding one is the on-switch); a SessionStart hook archives the previous sitting digest to .claude/kb/digests/ (still queryable) so now never inherits yesterday, and cues an unseeded project once. 0.9.0: the kb-scribe Stop hook is RETIRED — its enforcement now ships as the `session-digest` duty in the turn-end plugin, because two plugins each owning a blocking Stop hook re-armed each other (scribe counted the lens's mandated `Agent` dispatch as fresh work, and the resulting fix turn re-armed scribe). kb now carries TWO hooks (kb-pull, kb-session-start) + an MCP server — install kb itself; the bundle ships only its skills.

plugins.name: turn-end
plugins.description: The single blocking Stop hook, so nothing else needs one. Plugins ship turn-end DUTIES instead of their own hooks; one runner checks every applicable duty against real state and emits ONE consolidated message per user request — two duties become one tail with two items, never two tails. Exists because two plugins each owning a blocking Stop hook re-armed each other: each one's mandated response was fresh work for the other, so the allow-gap never landed on an idle turn (measured at 6 blocks + 3 fires in one sitting over ONE request, and 8 passes in another). All Stop hooks run in parallel with no ordering and blocking is fail-closed, so runtime negotiation between hooks is racy by construction; one runner has no race to lose. TERMINATION IS STRUCTURAL — a duty ends the loop by becoming satisfied against real state (the digest file exists, the agent was dispatched), never by a counter; the fire budget is only the backstop for a satisfaction check that is wrong, and it says so out loud when it gives up. Scoped to `prompt_id`, the user-request span, which is what turns an 8-pass session into 1. Escalation ladder: a first unmet duty gets hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (continues the turn, labelled Stop hook feedback, no hook error); only a duty marked severity:block, still unmet after that nudge, hardens to decision:block. Ships two duties — session-digest (from kb) and quality-lens (from verifiability-lens) — plus a judge adapter (`claude -p`, plan-billed, with the recursion guard the platform does not provide) for duties whose satisfaction is genuinely a matter of judgment; no shipped duty uses it, because every check answerable from disk stays on disk. Silent in a project with nothing to maintain, fail-open on every path, config off-switch. Add a duty = one require, no runner change. Carries a hook — install separately from the mk-cc-all bundle. 0.1.1: the quality-lens meta-loop guard now discriminates on the ROLLUP'S SHAPE (a bracketed tool marker, or two co-occurring structural tokens) rather than on the plugin's NAME — the inherited pattern matched the bare words "verifiability-lens", so the first live fire silently skipped the duty on a turn that merely discussed the lens. 0.2.0 adds the RECALL half — a second duty KIND that SUPPLIES material instead of demanding work. `context-recall` fires a `claude -p` judge on every turn end: it sees what was asked, what was answered, and an INDEX of the project's own notes (titles + ids, never bodies), returns which ones the answer should have been built on, and the runner then fetches those files deterministically and injects their own text. The judge chooses; it never summarises — so a session that re-derives a settled decision, repeats a rejected approach, or contradicts a recorded constraint gets the actual note back before it yields. Sources are the new extension surface (markdown-dir over kb captures/extracted and the steward model; a new instance is config, a new type is a drop-in). `supply` is the only impure step, so the pure runner just reports it is due and the adapter executes it — plan, execute, compose. Prompt-injection posture: the transcript is framed to the judge as data, not instructions. 0.3.0 adds a third duty, `steward-sync`: a living model is only worth what its last recompute was worth, and captures are cheap while the recompute is the expensive half nothing forced — a pilot model went a full session stale with every capture present and correct. It applies when `.steward/inbox/` holds a staged note and clears when the inbox is empty, the steward agent was dispatched, or it already asked this SITTING. Session span is load-bearing: its ask spawns a background agent, and an agent's completion wakes the session as a new prompt_id, so a prompt-span record would reset exactly when the dispatch paid off. What counts as an item is modelled rather than enumerated — a top-level non-dot `.md` file — so the `done/` archive and the permanent `.gitkeep` placeholder stay out of a count that would otherwise read 4 against a real inbox of 3 and never reach zero. New generic disk primitive `list(rel)` (typed, sorted, memoized with every other read); `hasFilesIn` now derives from it so the two cannot disagree about a tree.

plugins.name: mk-cc-all
plugins.description: All currently-active mk-cc-resources skills in one install: essense-flow, schema-scout, project-note-tracker, session-lifecycle, plugin-toolkit, kb skills. essense-autopilot, thorough-mode, alert-sounds, turn-end, reuse-gate, steward, and kb carry hooks and must be installed separately for their hook/MCP surfaces (the bundle ships kb's skills only). verifiability-lens no longer carries a hook — its automatic firing now comes from turn-end's quality-lens duty. statusline is neither (settings-level wiring — see its README). Benched plugins (miltiaze, ladder-build, architect, safe-commit, project-structure, repo-audit, mk-flow) are preserved on the archive/benched-plugins branch.
